summary: Independent source audit of Theorem AC. First, restricted my two earlier global claims ('no type-mixing version exists', 'neither premise follows from WeakColoring') to the two named finite countermodels actually exhibited: the four-state angular field, and the injective-choice configuration of three distinct 2-sets. Then audited AC against the Lean source. The four requested checks all pass: binary_strip_palette_rigidity takes only TWO open sets with a.e. confinement and no distinctness condition, so U = V = W is permitted; the radial sides are independent Booleans bu, bv; BinaryCenter is the hitting definition and the restriction lemmas produce exactly (palette x t inter J).Nonempty with J = {a,b}; and the finite widths are the source's own finite_positive_lower_bound over a Fintype, with W open by isOpen_iInter_of_finite. The boundary count checks too: D = angleBoundary is tau-invariant and nonempty, contains a six-point orbit with distinct points, yet sits inside B union (B - tau) with |B| = 2, so |D| <= 4 < 6. One overstatement corrected: the source takes INDIVIDUAL approach directions v i and needs only a common sign, so coincidence is forced by the boundary count needing |B| <= 2 - i.e. all v i on one common line. Hence the strongest nonaligned extension is (AC-axis) with possibly mixed orientations, which needs one missing lemma (a mixed-sign family restriction); for non-parallel directions |B| >= 4 and the count fails.

ApproachingContinuum x K v is a structure with x in K plus a sequence r n > 0 tending to 0, unit w n tending to v, and x + r n w n in K (235-242) - no reach or connectedness hypothesis is used or needed.

GRADE [S] ApproachingContinuum.outer_strip (244) gives, for 0 < <e,v>, a delta > 0 with the OUTER radial strip {x + r e' : 1 < r < 1+delta, dist e' e < delta} inside Straddle K; inner_strip (251) gives the INNER strip when <e,v> < 0. Both are then consumed by continuum_outer_restriction (259-278) and continuum_inner_restriction (279-300), which are stated for a FINITE family with INDIVIDUAL directions v i and conclude (palette x t inter J).Nonempty for a.e. t satisfying the common sign condition on the inner products.

GRADE [S] binary_strip_palette_rigidity (BoundaryTrace.lean:280-290) takes exactly two open sets U, V with a.e. confinement to {a,b} in each, a centre x, a direction t, delta > 0, and TWO INDEPENDENT Booleans bu, bv selecting the sides of the strips at directions t and t+pi/3; its conclusion is an i in {a,b} and an open angular neighbourhood A of t with i in the palette for a.e. u in A. Hence U = V = W is permitted (no distinctness or disjointness hypothesis), and the sides are independent - both checks pass.

GRADE [S] BinaryCenter x a b is the HITTING definition: for a.e. t, t in paletteSet x a or t in paletteSet x b (BinaryPalettes.lean:9); the restriction lemmas produce exactly the hitting statement with J = {a,b}, via the locally-a.e. gluing principle ae_of_locally_ae.

GRADE [S] The boundary count: angleEssential s b (334) is open, angleBoundary s is its complement-union (349), angleBoundary_shift (370) gives tau-invariance under the alternation, angleBoundary_nonempty (381) gives nonemptiness, angleBoundary_six (435) gives the full six-point orbit and sixAngle_injective (423) gives distinctness. So a nonempty tau-invariant D has at least 6 points, while D is contained in B union (B - tau) with |B| = 2 hence |D| <= 4. Contradiction.

GRADE [P] The restated theorem AC with exact hypotheses: measurable c, WeakColoring k c, a centre x, a unit vector v, a FINITE index type, ApproachingContinuum x (K i) v for all i, label sets H i with support j disjoint from Straddle (K i) for j in H i, and complement of the union of the H i of cardinality at most 2. Proof by the four steps, each consuming a named source lemma; the only k-dependence is that cardinality condition.

GRADE [P] The six-colour consumer checks arithmetically: q = (0,3,3,3,0,0) has edge label sets E1 = {1,2}, E2 = {2,3}, E3 = {3,4}, whose union is {1,2,3,4} and whose complement in Fin 6 is {0,5}, of size 2.

GRADE [P] The strongest nonaligned extension: the source needs no common direction, only a common sign of the inner products with the test direction; the exceptional set is then B = {t : some <direction t, v i> = 0} of size at most 2 per distinct axis, and the count needs |B| <= 2, i.e. all v i on one common line. So (AC-axis) with possibly mixed orientations is the maximal extension, and it needs one lemma not currently in the source: a mixed-sign family restriction. For non-parallel v i, |B| >= 4 gives |D| <= 8 which no longer contradicts |D| >= 6 - a quantitative limit of this method.
conjectures: The missing lemma for the mixed-orientation extension is a family version of binary_strip_palette_rigidity at the restriction stage: continuum_mixed_restriction, with a per-index choice of outer or inner strip and a single conclusion (palette x t inter J).Nonempty. If it exists, (AC-axis) follows with no other change.

The identity of the limiting quantity |D| <= 4 < 6 <= |D| suggests the method has no slack: any extension must keep the exceptional set at two points, so non-parallel approach directions cannot be covered by boundary counting alone and would need a different final step.
